popup.title: Endshift Tavern
popup.description: The Endshift Tavern was a frequent stop for off-duty members of the [[City Guard (Waterdeep)|City Guard]].

popup.title: Street of Lances
popup.description: Street of Lances was walked by broadcryers who peddled their broadsheets to passers-by.

popup.title: Seawind Alley
popup.description: Seawind Alley was an alley notable for the ghostly voices that could be heard within the alley.

popup.title: Ghostwalk
popup.description: Ghostwalk was considered sufficiently safe for the rich inhabitants of the ward to walk by undisturbed. Like other alleys in the Sea Ward, it was clean and wide. It contained numerous shadowtops that were favored by children to climb and play by.

popup.title: Westwall Street
popup.description: Westwall Street was located in the western section of Waterdeep's Sea Ward, fully spanning the entire western boundary of the ward with the exterior wall in that portion of the city.

popup.title: Heroes' Walk
popup.description: Every year during the summer, Heroes' Garden and Heroes' Walk were both overtaken by the nobles of the Church of Siamorphe on their holy day, the Divine Pageantry.

popup.title: Heroes' Garden
popup.description: Heroes' Garden was one of the only public gardens in the city besides the City of the Dead.

popup.title: Trollkill Street
popup.description: Trollkill Street was a large road in the city of Waterdeep, spanning nearly the whole northern portion of the Trollwall, that started in the Sea Ward and ended in the North Ward.

popup.title: Trollwall
popup.description: The Trollwall was a defensive barrier that encircled nearly the entirety of the city of Waterdeep.

popup.title: Street of the Singing Dolphin
popup.description: The Street of the Singing Dolphin was located in the western section of Waterdeep's Sea Ward. The road spanned the entire western side of the ward

popup.title: Oar Alley
popup.description: A minor avenue of hard-packed earth and [[gravel]] that extended off of [[Ship Street]] and terminated in a dead end.

popup.title: The Ship's Wheel
popup.description: The Ship's Wheel had a reputation for being one of the safest taverns around. Most activity within the tavern never got more exciting than the old patrons watching each others hair fall out.

popup.title: The Pilgrim's Rest
popup.description: This comfortable inn was moderately priced, at least by Waterdeep standards. Many of the patrons stayed here while visiting Waterdeep's temples. A private room could be had for 9 gp per night and included stabling and a meal.

popup.title: The Wandering Wemic
popup.description: Rooms could be had at the Wandering Wemic at a rate of 10 gp per night and included stabling, a valet service used for cleaning or repairing gear, and one bottle of wine per person per evening.

popup.title: Tchazzam Villa
popup.description: Tchazzam Villa was the family estate of the Waterdhavian noble house [[Tchazzam]].

popup.title: House of Inspired Hands
popup.description: The House of Inspired Hands was a temple of [[Gond]].

popup.title: Fiery Flagon
popup.description: The Fiery Flagon was a stately old tavern that served excellent food.

popup.title: House of Heroes
popup.description: The House of Heroes was a temple dedicated to the god [[Tempus]], the Lord of Battles. It was one of the biggest temples in Waterdeep.

popup.title: House of the Moon
popup.description: The House of the Moon was a temple of [[Selûne]]. It was one of the largest temples in the city.

popup.title: Field of Triumph
popup.description:
The Field of Triumph was a large outdoor stadium.

The Field of Triumph was the venue for many public spectacles from late spring until late autumn, weather permitting. The Open Lord of Waterdeep used the Field as a public forum to give proclamations to the city.

popup.title: New Olamn
popup.description: The College of New Olamn, simply known as New Olamn, was a traditional bardic college

popup.title: Blackstaff Tower
popup.description: Blackstaff Tower (previously Arunsun Tower; renamed by Khelben in [[1322 DR]]) was the home of Khelben "Blackstaff" Arunsun in Waterdeep. The foreboding structure was one of the most recognizable landmarks in Waterdeep's [[Castle Ward]].

popup.title: Sahuagin Humbled
popup.description: The [[Walking Statue of Waterdeep]] known as the Sahuagin Humbled was originally the only Walking Statue visible in Waterdeep.

popup.title: Halazar's Fine Gems
popup.description: Halazar's Fine Gems was a jewelry shop. The finest gems could be found in the shop, expertly cut and presented in simple glass cases.

popup.title: Adarbrent Villa
popup.description: Adarbrent Villa was the family estate of the Waterdhavian noble house [[Adarbrent]].

popup.title: Market Hall
popup.description: Market Hall was the guildhall of the [[Council of Farmer-Grocers]].

popup.title: Trollfort
popup.description: This structure stood four stories tall and was directly connected to the city walls that surrounded the Field Ward.

popup.title: North Tower
popup.description: The North Tower, also known as the Trolltower, was a torchtower. It had all the features that were common among them. This included a debriefing room, a small armory, holding cells, storage rooms for the holding of evidence or confiscated items, some bedchambers, and some garderobes.

popup.title: Armory of Waterdeep
popup.description: This building was the armory of the [[City Guard]].

popup.title: Shrine of Silvanus
popup.description: The Shrines of Nature was a temple complex in Waterdeep dedicated to the worship of the deities Mielikki and Silvanus, as well as a garden. The shrine dedicated to Silvanus was known by many names, including Seatrees Shrine, the Green Garden, the Quiet Place, and Oakenshade House.

popup.title: The Lady's Hands
popup.description: The Shrines of Nature was a temple complex in Waterdeep dedicated to the worship of the deities Mielikki and Silvanus, as well as a garden. The shrine dedicated to Mielikki was commonly known as the Lady's Hand.

popup.title: Naingate

popup.title: The Sleeping Snake
popup.description: Rowdy tavern for dockhands and dancers, owner by [[Alard Belaerl]].

popup.title: Shipmasters' Hall
popup.description: Shipmasters' Hall was an inn.

popup.title: Selûne's Smile
popup.description: Selûne's Smile, also known as the Inn of the Crescent Moon, was a tavern and inn devoted to [[Selûne]]. Uniquely, it was established and run by an [[avatar]] of the goddess Selûne.

popup.title: Mariners' Hall
popup.description: The Mariners' Hall was the guildhall of the [[Master Mariners' Guild]].

popup.title: Torpus's Tannery
popup.description: Torpus's Tannery was a tannery owned by [[Torpus the Tanner]].

popup.title: League Hall
popup.description: League Hall was the guildhall of the [[League of Skinners & Tanners]].

popup.title: Butchers' Guildhall

popup.description: Telethar Leatherworks was a leather goods store owned and operated by [[Orgul Telethar]].

popup.title: Fellowship Warehouse
popup.description: The Fellowship Warehouse, also known as the Fish Warehouse, was a warehouse that was owned by the [[Fishmongers' Fellowship]].

popup.title: Smokehouse
popup.description: The Smokehouse was a smokehouse that was owned by the [[Fishmongers' Fellowship]].

popup.title: Cookhouse Hall
popup.description: Cookhouse Hall was a civic building.

popup.title: Jemuril's residence
popup.description: Jemuril's residence was a the home of a [[dwarf]] warrior named [[Jemuril]].

popup.title: The Red Gauntlet
popup.description: Food served here consisted mostly of dried fish, waybread, and rabbit-and-fowl stew. Drink consisted of a house wine. The fares were cheap in the Red Gauntlet with a plate of food running just 3 cp and a tankard 2 cp.

popup.title: East Torch Tower
popup.description: East Torch Tower was the formal name given to one of the major torchtowers of Waterdeep's [[Trollwall]].

popup.title: Gelfuril the Trader
popup.description: Gelfuril the Trader was an unusual shop that was owned by the merchant [[Gelfuril]] in the 14th century DR. It was a similar to a pawnshop, though its owner was adamant about it not being one.

popup.title: Copper Cup
popup.description: The Copper Cup was a [[festhall]].

popup.title: South Gate
popup.description: The South Gate was the southern point of entrance through the [[Trollwall]].

popup.title: Orm's Highbench
popup.description: Orm's Highbench was the headquarters of a trading company.

popup.title: Bellister's House
popup.description: Bellister's House was a storage warehouse that was privately owned by the business [[Bellister's Hand]] in the mid–14th century DR.

popup.title: Athal's Stables
popup.description: Athal's Stables were a stables. [[Mount]]s and gear related to them, such as [[bit and bridle|bits, bridles]], and [[saddle]]s, could be purchased here.

popup.title: Bellister's Hand
popup.description: Bellister's Hand was a store. This business sold general goods. It was also possible to find stolen goods here.

popup.title: Melgard's Fine Leathers
popup.description: Melgard's Fine Leathers was a clothing store.

popup.title: Thomm Warehouse
popup.description: The Thomm Warehouse was a storage warehouse that was privately owned by [[Haerlit Thomm]] in the mid–14th century DR.

popup.title: Pelauvir's Counter
popup.description: Pelauvir's Counter was a general store and the site of a former warehouse.

popup.title: Deepwater Harbor
popup.description: Thanks to continuous efforts by the [[Guild of Watermen]] and its [[merfolk]] population, the cold waters of Deepwater Harbor were exceptionally clean.

popup.title: Deepwater Isle
popup.description: Deepwater was the largest in a ring of islands that enclosed and protected [[Deepwater Harbor]].

popup.title: T'Quession
popup.description: T'Quession was a [[sea elf]] hamlet.

popup.title: Naval Harbor
popup.description: The fleet of Waterdeep's navy was based in the Naval Harbor. Commercial and personal vessels were not permitted in this area.

popup.title: Harborwatch Tower
popup.description: Harborwatch Tower was one of the major torchtowers of Waterdeep's [[Trollwall]].

popup.title: Yawning Portal
popup.description: The Yawning Portal inn gained most of its renown for being the primary open route to the [[Undermountain]].

popup.title: Bell Tower
popup.description: A municipal bell tower that was used to signal the presence of fires, attacks on the city, or call for assemblies at [[Piergeiron's Palace]].

popup.title: Bowels of the Earth
popup.description: The tavern was a well-known spot for hiring [[mercenaries]].

popup.title: Rearing Hippocampus
popup.description: The Rearing Hippocampus was an inn.

popup.title: Turnstone Plumbing and Pipefitting
popup.description: Turnstone Plumbing and Pipefitting was a plumbing business that was owned by [[Jhalossan Turnstone]].

popup.title: The Blackstar Inn
popup.description: The Blackstar Inn was owned by [[Asiyra Boldwinter]] during the mid-to-late 14th century DR. Armed guards protected the entryway and the stables.

popup.title: Metal House of Wonders
popup.description: Metal House of Wonders was the guildhall of the [[Splendid Order of Armorers, Locksmiths, and Finesmiths]].

popup.title: Philosopher's Court
popup.description: Also known as the Foolsquare

popup.title: Stone House
popup.description: The Stone House was the guildhall of the [[Carpenters', Roofers', & Plaisterers' Guild]].

popup.title: Gray Serpent
popup.description: The Gray Serpent, which was also seen as the Grey Serpent, was an inn located in Waterdeep during the mid-to-late 14th century DR.

popup.title: Swords' Rest
popup.description: Swords' Rest was a tavern and a good place to hire [[mercenaries]].

popup.title: Serpentil Books & Folios
popup.description: Serpentil Books & Folios was a [[book]] shop.

popup.title: Cobblers' & Corvisers' House
popup.description: The Cobblers' and Corvisers' House was the guildhall of the [[Order of Cobblers & Corvisers]].

popup.title: Burdag Lane
popup.description: An entrance to the sewers of Waterdeep could be found on the intersection of Burdag Lane and Tsarnen Alley.

popup.title: Tsarnen Alley
popup.description: Tsarnen Alley was a short, hard-packed dirt and gravel paved, alleyway. It was frequently walked down by pilgrims and priests on their way to the [[Plinth]].

popup.title: Plinth
popup.description: The Plinth was a temple for all faiths and was the only temple located in the [[Trades Ward]].

popup.title: River Square
popup.description: River Square was a hard-packed dirt and gravel courtyard.

popup.title: Felzoun's Folly
popup.description: This tavern was frequently quite crowded and noisy, but overall was a casual place where merchants and consumers alike stopped for a quick bite or drink.

popup.title: Surtlan's Metalwares
popup.description: Surtlan's Metalwares sold metal products and equipment. It was owned by [[Baerhar Surtlan]] in the 14th century DR.

popup.title: Tornsar Alley
popup.description: Tornsar Alley was a small side alley.

popup.title: Juth Alley
popup.description: Juth Alley was a small side alley.

popup.title: House of Good Spirits
popup.description: The House of Good Spirits was the guildhall of the [[Vintners', Distillers', & Brewers' Guild]].

popup.title: Coach & Wagon Hall
popup.description: The Coach & Wagon Hall was the headquarters of the [[Wagonmakers' and Coach Builders' Guild]].

popup.title: Saddlers' & Harness-Makers' Hall
popup.description: The Saddlers' & Harness-Makers Hall, also known simply as the Saddlers' Hall, was the headquarters of the [[Saddlers' and Harness-makers' Guild]].

popup.title: River Gate
popup.description: The River Gate was the eastern point of entrance through the [[Trollwall]] into Waterdeep.

popup.title: Wheel Hall
popup.description: Wheel Hall was the guildhall of the [[Weelwrights' Guild]].

popup.title: The Redbridle Stables
popup.description: The Redbridle Stables were a stables that was owned by [[Rhazbos Redbridle]]. [[Mount]]s and gear related to them, such as [[bit and bridle|bits, bridles]], and [[saddle]]s, could be purchased here.

popup.title: Shipwrights' House
popup.description: Shipwrights' House was the guildhall of the [[Order of Master Shipwrights]].

popup.title: Helmstar Warehouse
popup.description: The Helmstar Warehouse was an old storage warehouse that was privately owned by [[Chuldan Helmstar]] in the mid–14th century DR.

popup.title: Ship's Prow
popup.description: The inn's name derived from the fact that it was converted into a building from the prow of a ship.

popup.title: Red Sails Warehouse
popup.description: The Red Sails Warehouse was a public storage warehouse.

popup.title: The Mermaid's Arms
popup.description: The Mermaid's Arms was a pricey and busy tavern, inn, and festhall.

popup.title: Arnagus the Shipwright
popup.description: This was a large shipbuilding shed owned by [[Arnagus the Shipwright]].

popup.title: Shipwright's Square
popup.description: Shipwright's Square was a small courtyard.

popup.title: Full Sails
popup.description: The Full Sails was a tavern that doubled as the guildhall of the [[Most Diligent League of Sail-Makers and Cordwainers]].

popup.title: Blue Mermaid
popup.description: The tavern was well appointed and clean, if a bit tired.

popup.title: Shippers' Hall
popup.description: The Shippers' Hall was the guildhall of the [[Fellowship of Salters, Packers, and Joiners]].

popup.title: Coopers' Rest
popup.description: Coopers' Rest was the guildhall of the [[Coopers' Guild]].

popup.title: Hanging Lantern
popup.description: The Hanging Lantern was a [[festhall]]. The building stood an impressive six storys tall.

popup.title: Sleeping Wench
popup.description: This tavern could be rather rowdy, but less so compared to the [[Sleeping Snake]] and had a comparably better clientele.

popup.title: Thirsty Sailor
popup.description: The Thirsty Sailor was an infamous dive bar.

popup.title: Warm Beds
popup.description: Warm Beds was an [[inn]].

popup.title: Lanternmaker Zorth Ulmaril
popup.description: Lanternmaker Zorth Ulmaril's shop was owned by its namesake, [[Zorth Ulmaril]].

popup.title: Bloody Fist
popup.description: The Bloody Fist was a [[tavern]].

popup.title: Hanged Man
popup.description: This tavern offered a fine selection of [[wine]]s, far better than one might suspect it to have, as well as a wide variety of [[ale]]s.

popup.title: Seaswealth Hall
popup.description: Seaswealth Hall was the guildhall of the [[Fishmongers' Fellowship]].

popup.title: Three Pearls Nightclub
popup.description: The Three Pearls Nightclub was a [[festhall]] and nightclub.

popup.title: Ghemmer's Alley
popup.description: Ghemmer's Alley was a small backalley.

popup.title: Purple Palace
popup.description: The Purple Palace was a [[festhall]].

popup.title: Thirsty Throat
popup.description: The Thirsty Throat was a [[tavern]].

popup.title: House of Pride
popup.description: House of Pride was a [[perfume]] shop.

popup.title: Fine Nuts
popup.description: Fine Nuts, which was also called Khostal Hannass Fine Nuts, was a shop.

popup.title: Felhaur's Fine Fish
popup.description: Felhaur's Fine Fish was a [[fish]] store. There were persistent rumors that the proprietor of this establishment was involved in smuggling.

popup.title: Blushing Mermaid
popup.description: The Blushing Mermaid was a tavern, inn, and festhall managed by Lady [[Alathene Moonstar]] circa the Year of Wild Magic, [[1372 DR]].

popup.title: Jade Dancer
popup.description: The Jade Dancer was a [[festhall]] and [[tavern]].

popup.title: Dancing Court
popup.description: The Dancing Court was a cul-de-sac.

popup.title: The Boomgarden
popup.description: The Boomgarden was a cul-de-sac, paved in hard-packed earth and gravel.

popup.title: Anchoret's Court
popup.description: Anchoret's Court was a small courtyard.

popup.title: Sethma's Court

popup.title: Nelkaush the Weaver
popup.description: Nelkaush the Weaver was a textiles shop.

popup.title: The Full Cup
popup.description: The Full Cup's patrons were mostly caravan drovers. Brawls were a common occurrence in this seedy [[tavern]].

popup.title: Hlakken Stables
popup.description: The Hlakken Stables were a stables. [[Mount]]s and gear related to them, such as [[bit and bridle|bits, bridles,]] and [[saddle]]s, could be purchased here.

popup.description: The Jar was a small courtyard.

popup.title: Old Monster Shop
popup.description: The shop specialized in [[poison]]s and other extraordinary items.

popup.title: Prestar's Furniture
popup.description: Prestar's Furniture was a furniture shop.

popup.title: Pampered Traveler
popup.description: Pampered Traveler was a fine establishment with large, well-furnished rooms, a play area for children, and a library that guests could peruse.

popup.title: Tower of the Order
popup.description: The Tower of the Order was the headquarters and seat of the [[Watchful Order of Magists and Protectors]].

popup.title: Inn of the Dripping Dagger
popup.description: The Inn of the Dripping Dagger was the favored bar and home to many adventurers, mercenaries, misfits and soldiers.

popup.title: Riven Shield Shop

popup.title: Mhair's Tower
popup.description: Mhair's Tower was the tower home of the wizard [[Mhair Szeltune]] in the 14th century DR.

popup.title: House of the Homeless
popup.description:
The House of the Homeless was a large mausoleum.

The dead of Waterdeep were interred within the House of the Homeless if they died without laying claim, or payment, to any other burial site.

popup.title: Merchants' Rest
popup.description: Merchants' Rest, which was also known as the Coinscoffin, was a tomb. Despite its name, Merchants' Rest was reserved for anyone, whether they were a merchant or not, who prepaid to be interred within.

popup.title: Warriors' Monument
popup.description: Warriors' Monument, also occasionally known as the Warriors of Waterdeep, was a monument in Waterdeep's [[City of the Dead]] meant to honor all those who ever fought to defend the city.

popup.title: Map House
popup.description: Map House was the guildhall of the [[Surveyors', Map & Chart-Makers' Guild]].

popup.title: House of Gems
popup.description: The House of Gems was the headquarters of the [[Jewelers' Guild]].

popup.description: Gondalim's was an [[inn]].

popup.title: Mistshore
popup.description: Mistshore was the name given to the dilapidated north shore of Waterdeep's harbor in the late 15th century DR.[

popup.title: Dock Ward
popup.description: The Dock Ward of Waterdeep was situated on the Great Harbor of Waterdeep. It contained the docks, shipbuilding yards, and warehouses for the sea trade. Compared to the rest of the city it was exceptionally dirty, smelly, and particularly dangerous.

popup.title: Southern Ward
popup.description: Southern Ward was the southeastern sector of the city of Waterdeep.

popup.title: Trades Ward
popup.description: The Trades Ward was one of the seven wards of the city of Waterdeep. It was the main shopping district of Waterdeep and housed many of the city's guildhalls.

popup.title: Castle Ward
popup.description: The Castle Ward was the central ward of the city of Waterdeep.

popup.title: Market
popup.description: The largest open area within the city was the marketplace between Trader's Way and Bazaar street. It was full of merchants carts and stalls both day and night and was the best place in the city to find a good price for any trade good found in Faerûn, assuming one had some skill at haggling.

popup.title: City of the Dead
popup.description: The City of the Dead was a large cemetery and ward in Waterdeep. Most of the city's dead were buried here. By day, it also doubled as the city's major public park picnic area.

popup.title: North Ward
popup.description: The North Ward was the northeastern sector of Waterdeep. It was famous for being the quietest ward of the city, consisting mostly of residential areas.

popup.title: Sea Ward
popup.description: The Sea Ward of Waterdeep was the wealthiest ward in Waterdeep and located in the northwest of the city.

popup.title: Field Ward
popup.description: The Field Ward of Waterdeep was an unofficial ward of the city, located between the inner and outer walls on the north side of town. It was in fact the city's slums — possessing the poorest living conditions within the city.

popup.title: Undercliff
popup.description: Undercliff was a rural community just outside the walls of Waterdeep, located east of the city proper. Along with the Field Ward, it was considered an unofficial ward of the city.

popup.title: Muleskull Tavern
popup.description: Muleskull Tavern was a tavern that doubled as the guildhall of the [[Dungsweepers' Guild]]

popup.title: Skewered Dragon
popup.description: The Skewered Dragon was a tavern. The clientele was primarily made up of dock workers that were suspicious of strangers.

popup.title: Steam and Steel
popup.description: Steam and Steel was a smithy. Operating during daylight hours, this smithy offered a wide variety of armors, shields, metal tools, and weaponry.

popup.title: Seven Masks Theater
popup.description: The Seven Masks Theater was a theater that catered to the masses typically found in the neighborhood. Ship captains and sailors were admitted for free.

popup.title: Nurneene's Marvelous Masks
popup.description: Nurneene's Marvelous Masks was a clothing boutique that sold stylish hand-made custom masks and costume accessories to the Waterdhavian elite.

Holyhands House was a temple to all deities.

This temple was once a villa that belonged to the [[Maernos]] noble family and was a bequeathal by the last of the Maernos line, [[Ultas Maernos]].
